title: Legacy basic-auth admin password password1234 must never bootstrap or log in an admin
answers: admin password1234 still works after upgrading MLflow basic auth
default admin credentials in basic_auth.ini are a security hole
how to stop the built-in admin account from using the published default password
MLflow basic-auth admin login accepted with known default password
body:
Symptom: Logging in as the built-in admin with the publicly documented password `password1234` succeeds, either on a fresh server or on an upgraded one.
Root cause: mlflow/server/auth/basic_auth.ini:admin_password shipped `password1234`, and create_admin_user used it as the bootstrap password.
Fix pattern: Remove the shipped default. Reject the legacy value in _validate_bootstrap_admin_password, and reject admin logins that present it via _is_disabled_legacy_admin_login, called from _authenticate_cached (before caching) and from authenticate_request_basic_auth on the Flask path.
Constraints: Only admin accounts are rejected; non-admin users with the same password still log in. Upgraded servers keep starting so the only admin is not locked out, so the startup warning from _warn_if_legacy_default_password_in_use is the only signal for operators. Any new credential-accepting path must call the same guard or the default credential reopens.
applies: Basic-auth (`--app-name basic-auth`) login and bootstrap paths in mlflow/server/auth.
says: The default administrator password still allows access after setting up authentication.
Security audit flags the built-in admin account for using a published default password.
Block administrator login attempts that use the known default password.
Prevent new tracking servers from initializing administrator accounts with default credentials.
Logging into the tracking server as administrator with default credentials is prohibited.
search: The legacy default password password1234 must never bootstrap or authenticate an admin account under --app-name basic-auth. The shipped default is removed from basic_auth.ini, rejected during bootstrap by _validate_bootstrap_admin_password, and blocked during login by _is_disabled_legacy_admin_login in _authenticate_cached and authenticate_request_basic_auth. This check applies only to admin accounts, and upgraded servers continue starting while logging a startup warning from _warn_if_legacy_default_password_in_use.
